merge_request.description:
Upgrading SQLAlchemy from 1.4.49 to 2.1.6 involved adapting to significant API shifts in query construction, execution patterns, and session management. The `select()` function now requires strictly positional column arguments, while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements no longer accept keyword-based constructors—both necessitated refactoring across database interaction code. Legacy methods like `Engine.execute()` and `Session.query()` were replaced with modern equivalents using `Connection.execute()` and `Session.execute(select())`, aligning with SQLAlchemy 2.0’s unified Core/ORM approach. The declarative base import moved from `sqlalchemy.ext.declarative` to `sqlalchemy.orm.declarative_base`, and enabling the `future=True` flag on `Session` activated autobegin behavior while removing subtransaction complexity. Result handling was updated to use `.scalars()` and `.unique()` for ORM object extraction, reflecting the new named-tuple-like row semantics. All changes were applied to `pyshop/db.py` and `requirements.txt`, and the full test suite passes, confirming stability and correctness under the new version. ## What changed - sqlalchemy 1.4.49 -> 2.1.6 in requirements.txt ## Code changes and why | File | Change | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `pyshop/db.py` | declarative_base moved from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative to sqlalchemy.orm in SQLAlchemy 2.0 (breaking change #6).
SQLAlchemy 2.0 requires select() columns to be passed positionally, not as a list (breaking changes #1 and #5).
Replace deprecated Query API with select() and Session.execute() pattern, using scalars() for ORM results.
Replace deprecated Query.get() with Session.get() per SQLAlchemy 2.0 migration guide. | [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#library-level-but-not-driver-level-autocommit-removed-from-both-core-and-orm) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#declarative-becomes-a-first-class-api) [source](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) | ## Documented changes that applied to this codebase - **breaking**: select() no longer accepts varied constructor arguments, columns passed positionally (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.select) > The list of columns / tables to SELECT from should be passed positionally, rather than as a list. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) - **breaking**: insert/update/delete DML no longer accept keyword constructor arguments (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.Integer, sqlalchemy.String) > The constructor arguments to insert(), update() and delete() other than the table argument are essentially removed. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#insert-update-delete-dml-no-longer-accept-keyword-constructor-arguments) - **breaking**: Engine.execute() considered legacy, use Connection.execute() or Session.execute() (sqlalchemy.create_engine) > The Engine.execute() method is considered legacy as of the 1.x series of SQLAlchemy and will be removed in 2.0. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#library-level-but-not-driver-level-autocommit-removed-from-both-core-and-orm) - **breaking**: Session.query() unified with Core select(), new Session.execute(select(...)) pattern (sqlalchemy.select) > The Query object becomes long term legacy, replaced by the direct usage of the select() construct in conjunction with the Session.execute() method. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#orm-query-unified-with-core-select) - **breaking**: select() legacy calling style deprecated, new positional style required (sqlalchemy.Column, sqlalchemy.select) > The list of columns / tables to SELECT from should be passed positionally, rather than as a list. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#select-no-longer-accepts-varied-constructor-arguments-columns-are-passed-positionally) - **breaking**: Declarative base import path changed from ext to orm (sqlalchemy.ext.declarative.declarative_base) > Change imports: from sqlalchemy.ext import declarative_base, declared_attr To: from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, declared_attr [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#declarative-becomes-a-first-class-api) - **breaking**: Session future flag enables autobegin, removes subtransactions (sqlalchemy.orm.sessionmaker) > The Session no longer supports 'bound metadata' when it resolves the engine to be used for connectivity. This means that an Engine object must be passed to the constructor. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#migration-to-2-0-step-five-use-the-future-flag-on-session) - **breaking**: Result rows act like named tuples, require .scalars()/.unique() for ORM results (sqlalchemy.select) > Result rows act like named tuples and it will not deduplicate results in memory. In order to return single ORM objects the way Query does, the Result.scalars() modifier must be called first. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#result-rows-act-like-named-tuples) - **deprecation**: RemovedIn20Warnings deprecation categories (noise until resolved) > Code can be developed iteratively to resolve these warnings. Enable SQLALCHEMY_WARN_20=1 environment variable. [↗](http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/changelog/migration_20.html#migration-to-2-0-step-two-turn-on-removedin20warnings) ## Verification - After the bare version bump: 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected - After Upshift's edits: **17 passing, 0 failing of 17 collected** | Attempt | Model | Edits | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 2 | 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected | | 2 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 1 | 15 passing, 2 failing of 17 collected | | 3 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 1 | 16 passing, 1 failing of 17 collected | | 4 | `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b` | 2 | 17 passing, 0 failing of 17 collected | ## Review Verdict: **approve**. All breaking changes from SQLAlchemy 1.4 → 2.1 are correctly addressed: select() uses positional columns, Engine.execute() replaced with Connection.execute() via engine.begin(), declarative_base import path updated, Query API migrated to select()+Session.execute() with scalars(), and Session.get() used directly. No weakened tests, behavior changes, compat shims, missed migrations, or security regressions found. Code quality is clean. ## Cost - Token Factory usage: $0.0767 across `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b`, `nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning` - Evidence sources: 5 pages (2 Tavily searches) --- Generated by [Upshift](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/43491832/nvidxnebi) with NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory. Every edit above links to the changelog or migration guide that justifies it; tests ran in an isolated sandbox.

Legacy methods like `Engine.execute()` and `Session.query()` were replaced with modern equivalents using `Connection.execute()` and `Session.execute(select())`, aligning with SQLAlchemy 2.0’s unified Core/ORM approach. The declarative base import moved from `sqlalchemy.ext.declarative` to `sqlalchemy.orm.declarative_base`, and enabling the `future=True` flag on `Session` activated autobegin behavior while removing subtransaction complexity. Result handling was updated to use `.scalars()` and `.unique()` for ORM object extraction, reflecting the new named-tuple-like row semantics.
